t: You're on Mortimer Street, in the City of Westminster. It runs from the junction with Cavendish Place, Langham Place and Regent Street in the west, to the junction with Cleveland Street, Goodge Street and Newman Street in the east. Several streets join it along the way, including Great Portland Street, Great Titchfield Street and Berners Street. It's named after Edward Harley, the second Earl of Oxford and Earl Mortimer, a Tory politician who sat in the House of Commons between 1711 and 1724.
